explanation: A king who ruled over Judea and was known for his brutality and paranoia.
An ancient North African country where the Israelites were held as slaves under Pharaoh's rule.
The supreme ruler of Egypt, often regarded as a divine figure.
A people who, according to the Bible, are God's chosen people, descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
A prophet and leader of the Israelites who helped them escape slavery in Egypt and led them through the wilderness toward the promised land.
Ten disasters that God brought upon the Egyptians to force Pharaoh to let the Israelites go.
A divine figure sent by God to kill all the firstborn in Egypt as punishment for their treatment of the Israelites.

A Jewish festival celebrating the Israelites' deliverance from slavery in Egypt. Passover gets its name from God's command that the Israelites should smear the blood of a sacrificial lamb on their doorposts, so that the Angel of Death would "pass over" their homes and not kill their firstborn.
An animal sacrificed by the Israelites as part of the Passover ritual, whose blood was used to protect their firstborn.
The oldest child in a family, who held special status and rights in ancient society.
